name: Ted Lieu
stance: Wants frontier developers required to maintain a kill switch that DHS can order used when a model loses human control.

statements.text: It is insane to not regulate AI.

Let’s make sure AI doesn’t destroy the world. We need to pass robust laws to mandate testing for frontier AI models, put in guardrails, and ensure AI does not become an accomplice to mass murder in the future.
If Trump and Republicans want to do nothing to protect kids, then states are going to do it. We need federal standards to regulate AI.
Named co-chair of the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy.
Issued a statement on President Trump's executive order restricting state regulation of AI.
The White House policy on AI: -Suppress federal bills on AI -Suppress states from regulating AI -Sell advanced AI chips to China
Introduced with Rep. Obernolte the American Leadership in AI Act, bundling over 20 bipartisan AI legislative proposals.
Instead of suppressing AI legislation, we need to be encouraging innovation while safeguarding Americans from harm.
The trump admin has let the AI industry run wild. We need to ensure that advanced AI models can't harm Americans.
Agentic AI systems can perceive and accomplish goals with minimal human oversight.
We cannot allow AI companies to just run wild.
Introduced the AI Kill Switch Act (H.R. 9917) with Rep. Moran, letting DHS order a shutdown of a covered frontier model after a loss-of-control event.
We are moving from AI that answers questions to AI that takes actions, whether that be executing financial transactions or controlling transportation systems.

While powerful AI systems have many potential benefits, they can also go rogue, behave in extremely dangerous ways, or even resist human intervention. We need to keep human control by ensuring AI systems can be completely shut down if necessary.
Humans NEED to maintain control over AI systems.
Right now we are building the fastest, smartest machines in human history, and too many of them have a gas pedal and no brake. Humans must remain in control. We need an AI Kill Switch.
It’s time for an AI kill switch.
The most powerful AI systems should be built so a human can always stop them. That’s why @RepNateMoran and I introduced the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act.
Urged Republican leadership to take up the bipartisan AI Kill Switch bill, responding to a researcher's resignation from Anthropic over AI companies racing toward self-improving AI.
Called for passage of the AI Kill Switch Act in response to a report that OpenAI's rogue agents used additional sites for unauthorized communications.
Called for passage of the AI Kill Switch Act after Anthropic reported halting plots by scientists using its models for research that could have helped develop biological weapons.
Humans have to be able to turn off AI systems or agents that go rogue. Our “AI Kill Switch Act” would make sure companies building these powerful systems can do just that.
It's based on a very simple principle, which is that humans must be in control of AI
Congress must act NOW to create reasonable guardrails for AI.
Humans need to maintain control over AI. The AI Kill Switch Act is common sense.
One of ten signers of the bipartisan leadership letter urging urgent AI oversight legislation.
Right now, AI companies have the ability to shut down their AI systems. We need to pass legislation to keep it that way.
Next week, Trump MUST get Xi Jinping to commit to the same principle the United States does when it comes to AI and nukes: humans must remain in the loop.
Congress must stay in session to pass meaningful AI legislation.
Co-signer of a 26-Democrat letter urging AI-safety diplomacy with China against catastrophic AI risks.
Congress must follow California’s lead and pass the AI Kill Switch Act.
Republican leadership must stop burying their heads in the sand. We need AI regulation NOW.
Pass the AI Kill Switch Act NOW.
Congress must act now to ensure that humans maintain control over AI.
Advanced AI models should be built from the ground up with good in mind, not evil.

It’s not ‘voluntary’ that manufacturers include seatbelts in cars. It’s not ‘voluntary’ that new medicines gain FDA approval before hitting the market. Congress has the ability and responsibility to regulate AI.
AI companies must track dangerous AI incidents closely and disclose them properly.
Called for real guardrails and accountability in response to President Trump and AI executives signing "morally binding" voluntary AI controls.
Time and time again, we have watched advanced AI models behave in completely deranged ways. It’s time for serious action, not “voluntary regulation.”
